title: Serre regularity in codimension ascends along flat maps with regular fibres
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $k\ge0$ an integer. Assume that $R$ and $S$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], that $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the fibre ring $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] (a Noetherian ring) has property $(R_k)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk], and that $R$ has property $(R_k)$. Then $S$ has property $(R_k)$; that is, $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$ of height at most $k$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 033A (lemma-Rk-goes-up, line 46460); property (R_k): Definition definition-conditions (line 43872)

proof.text: *Setting.* Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal of height at most $k$; by [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk] we must show that $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring. Put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, a prime ideal of $R$, so $\mathfrak q$ lies over $\mathfrak p$. The height of $\mathfrak q$ is $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk], so $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}\le k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] (with $\varphi$ flat), the induced map $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$, $r/s\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(s)$, is a flat local homomorphism, and, $R$ and $S$ being Noetherian, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S_{\mathfrak q}$ are Noetherian local rings.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 033A (lemma-Rk-goes-up), proof, lines 46474-46487: 'Let q be a prime of S lying over a prime p of R. Assume that dim(S_q) <= k.'

proof.text: *Base height bound.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] in its height form: ht(q) = ht(p) + ht(q/pS), using flat going down and the instance that q lies over its contraction p. Nonnegativity of heights gives ht(p) <= ht(q) <= k. This is `Ideal.height_eq_height_add_of_liesOver_of_hasGoingDown p q` followed by `le_self_add` in Lean.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 033A (lemma-Rk-goes-up), proof, lines 46474-46487: 'Since dim(S_q) = dim(R_p) + dim(S_q/pS_q) by Lemma lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total (Tag 00ON) we see that dim(R_p) <= k and dim(S_q/pS_q) <= k.'

proof.text: *$R_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular.* $\dim R_{\mathfrak p}$ is the height of $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk], which is $\le k$ by Step 2. Since $R$ has property $(R_k)$, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 033A (lemma-Rk-goes-up), proof, lines 46474-46487: 'Hence R_p ... [is] regular by assumption.'

proof.text: *Regular closed fibre.* Obtain Noetherianity and (R_k) of C = kappa(p) tensor_R S directly from the fibre hypothesis; [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-noetherian] is unnecessary. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection], choose Q in Spec C contracting to q, using `PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber` and its left inverse. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-local-ring-iso], `Ideal.Fiber.algEquivAux₂ p Q` identifies C_Q with S_q / pS_q. Transport along the equality of the contracted prime with q (the local `transport` equality-elimination proof) and the closed-fibre ideal equality of Step 5. A quotient cannot increase Krull dimension: chains of primes pull back along its surjection preserving strict inclusions; Mathlib `ringKrullDim_quotient_le` gives this in one line. Together with `ringKrullDim_eq_of_ringEquiv` and `IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height`, this gives ht(Q) = dim(C_Q) <= dim(S_q) = ht(q) <= k. Apply (R_k) of C at Q, then transport regularity using `IsRegularLocalRing.of_ringEquiv`.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 033A (lemma-Rk-goes-up), proof, lines 46474-46487: 'Hence ... S_q/pS_q [is] regular by assumption', with Remark Tag 0H9M (remark-local-ring-fibre, line 3520) identifying S_q/pS_q with the local ring of the fibre ring S (x)_R kappa(p) at the prime corresponding to q (the source leaves this identification implicit)

proof.text: *Closed fibre ideal equality.* Let f = Localization.localRingHom p q (algebraMap R S) rfl and J = (maximalIdeal R_p).map f. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], `IsLocalization.AtPrime.map_eq_maximalIdeal p` expresses the base maximal ideal as the image of p. Rewrite both iterated ideal maps with `Ideal.map_map`. The two resulting maps R -> S_q agree on every x by `Localization.localRingHom_to_map`. Hence J = (p.map (algebraMap R S)).map (algebraMap S S_q), exactly the ideal in `Ideal.Fiber.algEquivAux₂`. This proves the identification with the closed fibre without any new statement.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 033A (lemma-Rk-goes-up), proof, lines 46474-46487 (the identification of S_q/pS_q with the closed fibre of R_p -> S_q, implicit in the application of Tag 031E)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* $\varphi_{\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings (Step 1), $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular (Step 3), and its closed fibre $S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak m_{R_{\mathfrak p}}S_{\mathfrak q}=S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}$ (Step 5) is regular (Step 4). By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre] (Stacks 031E), $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring. As $\mathfrak q$ was an arbitrary prime of height $\le k$, $S$ has property $(R_k)$ [def-weil-pbc-serre-conditions-rk-sk].
